addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	import { defineSchema, defineTable } from "convex/server";
2	import { v } from "convex/values";
3	
4	export default defineSchema({
5	  people: defineTable({
6	    // Clerk's identity.tokenIdentifier ("issuer|subject"); the stable
7	    // ownership key now that there is no local users table.
8	    userId: v.string(),
9	    name: v.string(),
10	    // Accent-insensitive lowercase key for search_normalized_name; see
11	    // nameSearch.ts. Optional because rows created before this field
12	    // existed (and rows captures.ts inserts directly) need a backfill --
13	    // see backfillNormalizedNames in people.ts.
14	    normalizedName: v.optional(v.string()),
15	    link: v.optional(v.string()),
16	    context: v.optional(v.string()),
17	    updatedAt: v.number(),
18	    // Captured-from-screenshot provenance; all optional so hand-added
19	    // people need no migration.
20	    platform: v.optional(v.string()),
21	    handle: v.optional(v.string()),
22	    headline: v.optional(v.string()),
23	    screenshotId: v.optional(v.id("_storage")),
24	    // Haven Meet provenance. Each side still gets a private people row; this
25	    // key only lets a repeat in-person exchange stay idempotent.
26	    eunoContactUserId: v.optional(v.string()),
27	    // Semantic search. embeddedText doubles as the idempotency key so the
28	    // embed action can skip recomputing an unchanged person.
29	    embedding: v.optional(v.array(v.float64())),
30	    embeddedText: v.optional(v.string()),
31	  })
32	    .index("by_user", ["userId"])
33	    .index("by_user_and_eunoContactUserId", ["userId", "eunoContactUserId"])
34	    // Same reasoning as captures.by_screenshotId: the orphaned-upload sweep
35	    // needs a sound, bounded way to check "is this blob referenced?".
36	    .index("by_screenshotId", ["screenshotId"])
37	    .searchIndex("search_normalized_name", {
38	      searchField: "normalizedName",
39	      filterFields: ["userId"],
40	    })
41	    .vectorIndex("by_embedding", {
42	      vectorField: "embedding",
43	      dimensions: 1536,
44	      filterFields: ["userId"],
45	    }),
46	  // A future mutual-link flow should create one row only after both Haven users
47	  // have explicitly connected. Each side binds the relationship to their own
48	  // private person row; the shared-note API uses this as its access gate.
49	  connections: defineTable({
50	    userAId: v.string(),
51	    userBId: v.string(),
52	    personAId: v.id("people"),
53	    personBId: v.id("people"),
54	    status: v.literal("connected"),
55	    createdAt: v.number(),
56	    updatedAt: v.number(),
57	  })
58	    .index("by_userAId_and_personAId", ["userAId", "personAId"])
59	    .index("by_userBId_and_personBId", ["userBId", "personBId"])
60	    .index("by_userAId_and_userBId", ["userAId", "userBId"]),
61	  sharedNotes: defineTable({
62	    connectionId: v.id("connections"),
63	    content: v.optional(v.string()),
64	    updatedAt: v.number(),
65	    updatedByUserId: v.string(),
66	  }).index("by_connectionId", ["connectionId"]),
67	  // A screenshot waiting to be triaged into a person. Deleted on accept
68	  // (the file moves to the person) or discard (the file is deleted too).
69	  captures: defineTable({
70	    userId: v.string(),
71	    screenshotId: v.id("_storage"),
72	    status: v.union(
73	      v.literal("pending"),
74	      v.literal("ready"),
75	      v.literal("failed"),
76	    ),
77	    extracted: v.optional(
78	      v.object({
79	        platform: v.string(),
80	        name: v.string(),
81	        handle: v.optional(v.string()),
82	        headline: v.optional(v.string()),
83	        bio: v.optional(v.string()),
84	      }),
85	    ),
86	    // Short, generic, user-safe message. Never the raw upstream text.
87	    error: v.optional(v.string()),
88	    // Raw upstream/error text for our own debugging. Never returned to a
89	    // client -- listCaptures and getCapture must not project this field.
90	    errorDetail: v.optional(v.string()),
91	  })
92	    .index("by_user", ["userId"])
93	    // Lets the stuck-pending sweep find old "pending" rows without a table
94	    // scan; Convex appends _creationTime as the trailing key, so this index
95	    // also supports the age cutoff range on the same query.
96	    .index("by_status", ["status"])
97	    // Lets the orphaned-upload sweep check "is this blob referenced?" as an
98	    // exact indexed lookup per candidate instead of a bounded table scan --
99	    // see sweepOrphanedUploads in captures.ts for why that matters for
100	    // soundness.
101	    .index("by_screenshotId", ["screenshotId"]),
102	  // Fixed-window per-user rate limiting. One row per (userId, action) pair;
103	  // an action name like "createCapture:minute" models one window, so a
104	  // function with two windows (e.g. per-minute and per-day) gets two rows.
105	  rateLimits: defineTable({
106	    userId: v.string(),
107	    action: v.string(),
108	    windowStart: v.number(),
109	    count: v.number(),
110	  }).index("by_user_action", ["userId", "action"]),
111	
112	  // A user's public-in-the-moment Haven handle. This is not a social profile:
113	  // it exists only so two people standing together can intentionally exchange.
114	  profiles: defineTable({
115	    userId: v.string(),
116	    username: v.string(),
117	    updatedAt: v.number(),
118	  })
119	    .index("by_user", ["userId"])
120	    .index("by_username", ["username"]),
121	
122	  // Opt-in, short-lived proximity sessions for Love Alarm. Kept separate from
123	  // people because heartbeats are intentionally high-churn operational data.
124	  loveAlarmPresence: defineTable({
125	    userId: v.string(),
126	    roomCode: v.string(),
127	    displayName: v.string(),
128	    joinedAt: v.number(),
129	    lastSeenAt: v.number(),
130	    expiresAt: v.number(),
131	  })
132	    .index("by_userId_and_roomCode", ["userId", "roomCode"])
133	    .index("by_userId_and_expiresAt", ["userId", "expiresAt"])
134	    .index("by_roomCode_and_expiresAt", ["roomCode", "expiresAt"]),
135	
136	  // Cursor state for paginated background sweeps: without a persisted
137	  // watermark a bounded sweep re-reads the same head of the table forever
138	  // and never progresses past rows it must skip.
139	  sweepState: defineTable({
140	    key: v.string(),
141	    watermark: v.number(),
142	  }).index("by_key", ["key"]),
143	
144	  // Public waitlist signups from the /#/join landing. No auth: these are
145	  // strangers, not users. Email is stored normalized (trimmed + lowercased)
146	  // so by_email gives an exact dedupe lookup. `source` records which
147	  // responsive layout they joined from. _creationTime is the signup time.
148	  // `name` is required by the joinWaitlist mutation for every new signup, but
149	  // stays optional in the schema because rows created before this field
150	  // existed have none -- same reasoning as people.normalizedName above.
151	  waitlist: defineTable({
152	    name: v.optional(v.string()),
153	    email: v.string(),
154	    source: v.union(v.literal("desktop"), v.literal("phone")),
155	  }).index("by_email", ["email"]),
156	});

content.text:
Reviewed every touched file in full. All + lines are cosmetic rebranding (Euno → Haven / eunomious.vercel.app → inhavens.com):

- **emailClient.ts**: Only string literals change. `renderConfirmation` still escapes `name` via `escapeHtml` before interpolating into HTML at line 53, and still passes the raw `name` into the plain-text greeting (line 32) — which is safe because plain-text has no markup context (comment on line 26 confirms the intent). No sink or trust change.
- **emailClient.test.ts**: Only assertion strings updated to match the rebrand.
- **openaiClient.ts**: One-word comment change; no code change.
- **profiles.ts**: `ensureMeetPerson` context/platform string and two `throw new Error` messages rebranded. No auth/gate/query logic touched.
- **profiles.test.ts**: Only expected-string rebrand.
- **schema.ts**: Only comments; field names (including `eunoContactUserId`) preserved, so no index-name or registry drift.
- **index.html**: Static meta tags, icon SVG, and title. `og:url` moved to `https://inhavens.com/`; preconnects to Clerk/Convex hosts unchanged. `img.ogis.dev` was already used pre-change, and the interpolated `title`/`description` query params are static literals, not user input.

No source→sink path is added, no validator/allowlist/gate is modified, no secret/PII is added to a log or error message, no permission is granted, no new registry key is added that other files must mirror.
